newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-HK Newspaper Headlines-March 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-HK Newspaper Headlines-March 21.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- Ottawa announced visa-free access to Canada for holders of Hong Kong Special Aministrative Region passports, but warned that the decision might be withdrawn if there was an increase inflow of illegal immigrants from the territory.
-- SING TAO -- The British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind vowed that Britain would monitor the Hong Kong Special Adminstrative Region until the year 2000.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Beijing urged Britain to cooperate with China on Hong Kong affairs and make good preparations for the handover in the remaining 100 days under British rule.
-- Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa said education should be strengthened to raise Hong Kong's younger generation's sense of being Chinese.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- Head of the Home Affairs department of Hong Kong urged China to give priorities to mainland applicants who needed to emigrate to the territory to reunite with their families, when handling immigration applications.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- A study by an influential thinktank in Beijing concluded Sino-U.S. relations would continue to be hobbled by developments in domestic U.S. politics.
-- Jardine Matheson Holdings said it had taken a US$26 million charge to cover itself against last year's trading scandal at Jardine Fleming, its 50 per cent-owned investment banking joint venture.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Three special task forces to be announced by Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa are likely to create conflict in the Civil Service. Observers say Tung's move could put senior officials in a subordinate position.
-- Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings surpassed market expectations by posting a strong 56 per cent jump in net profits to $886 million.
